preconditions.description: The number of nodes n must be between 3 and 100000.
The number of edges m must be between 3 and 100000.
The lower limit on the degree k must be between 2 and n-1.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b for a, b in edges)
preconditions.description: All edges must connect distinct nodes within the range of 1 to n.

postconditions.description: The first line of output must be the length of the found cycle.
The length of the found cycle must be at least k + 1.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= v <= n for v in cycle)
postconditions.description: All nodes in the cycle must be valid node indices between 1 and n.
All nodes in the cycle must be distinct.

postconditions.expression: all((cycle[i], cycle[i+1]) in edges or (cycle[i+1], cycle[i]) in edges for i in range(len(cycle)-1)) and ((cycle[-1], cycle[0]) in edges or (cycle[0], cycle[-1]) in edges)

repair_issue.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure the cycle forms a valid simple cycle by checking that consecutive nodes in the cycle are connected by edges and the first and last nodes are also connected.
repair_issue.task_evidence: A simple cycle of length d (d > 1) in graph G is a sequence of distinct graph nodes v_1, v_2, ..., v_{d} such, that nodes v_1 and v_{d} are connected by an edge of the graph, also for any integer i (1 ≤ i < d) nodes v_{i} and v_{i} + 1 are connected by an edge of the graph.
